checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is Fiat-Shamir hash input serialization in compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge (SG-006) deterministic and canonical across all client implementations?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the hash computation in compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge (SG-006). 2. Verify the serialization order strictly follows: domain, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL, len(commitments), len(cell_indices), commitments, then for each k: commitment_indices[k], cell_indices[k], coset_evals[k], proofs[k]. 3. Cross-compare serialization implementations across multiple Ethereum clients (Prysm, Lighthouse, Teku, Lodestar, Nimbus). 4. Construct identical batch verification inputs and verify all clients produce identical Fiat-Shamir challenge values (r). 5. Test edge cases: empty commitments array, single commitment, maximum allowed commitments. 6. Verify endianness consistency for all integer serializations.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0011, Trust Boundary: tb-006, Primary Element: SG-006. Non-deterministic Fiat-Shamir challenge computation is a consensus-critical vulnerability. Different challenges produce different batch verification results for identical inputs.

checklist.title: Verify Fiat-Shamir Oracle Input Handling: Does actor-fiat-shamir-oracle produce identical challenge values for identical serialized inputs across all code paths?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace all call sites to compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge. 2. Verify no caching or memoization could produce stale challenge values. 3. Confirm no floating-point or non-deterministic operations exist in the hash input construction. 4. Test with intentionally duplicated inputs to verify idempotency. 5. Verify the hash domain separator is unique to this function to prevent cross-protocol attacks.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0011, Covered Node: actor-fiat-shamir-oracle. The Fiat-Shamir transformation security relies on deterministic challenge computation.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does polynomial_eval_to_coeff (SG-007) strictly reject inputs with length != FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the polynomial_eval_to_coeff function (SG-007). 2. Verify an explicit length check exists at function entry: assert(len(evaluations) == FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB). 3. Test with input lengths: 0, 1, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB - 1, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB + 1, 2 * FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. 4. Verify all non-conforming lengths are rejected with appropriate errors. 5. Trace upstream callers (blob_to_polynomial) to verify they cannot pass non-standard lengths. 6. Review for any implicit truncation or zero-padding that might silently accept wrong lengths.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0012, Trust Boundary: tb-002/tb-003, Primary Element: SG-007. Accepting wrong-length inputs produces polynomials of incorrect degree, invalidating all subsequent KZG operations.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is bit_reversal_permutation applied BEFORE inverse FFT in polynomial_eval_to_coeff (SG-007)?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate polynomial_eval_to_coeff (SG-007) implementation. 2. Verify the operation sequence is: (a) receive evaluations, (b) apply bit_reversal_permutation, (c) perform inverse FFT. 3. Compare against the spec pseudocode to confirm ordering. 4. Test with known test vectors: apply function to canonical blob data and verify output matches expected coefficient representation. 5. Cross-compare encoding (SG-007) and decoding (SG-023 recovery) paths to verify consistent bit-reversal usage. 6. Check for any conditional branches that might skip bit-reversal for certain inputs.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0013, Trust Boundary: tb-003, Primary Element: SG-007. Incorrect bit-reversal ordering produces wrong coefficients for every blob, causing all generated proofs to fail verification on correctly-implemented clients.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does multiply_polynomialcoeff (SG-009) assert len(a) + len(b) <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB before multiplication?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the multiply_polynomialcoeff function (SG-009). 2. Verify an explicit assertion exists at function entry: assert(len(a) + len(b) <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB). 3. Test with polynomials of degrees: (deg(a)=0, deg(b)=0), (deg(a)=FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 - 1, deg(b)=FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2), (deg(a) + deg(b) = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB), (deg(a) + deg(b) > FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB). 4. Verify the last case is rejected with an appropriate error. 5. Trace callers from recovery path (SG-023) to identify how attacker-supplied cells determine polynomial degrees. 6. Construct a recovery scenario where crafted cell data would cause degree overflow if the check is missing.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0015, Trust Boundary: tb-003, Primary Element: SG-009. Exceeding FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB degree produces polynomials outside trusted setup support, causing incorrect/exploitable KZG commitments.

checklist.title: Verify Product Polynomial Degree: Does multiply_polynomialcoeff (SG-009) guarantee result degree equals deg(a) + deg(b)?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the polynomial multiplication algorithm for correctness. 2. Verify result array is allocated with size len(a) + len(b) - 1 (= deg(a) + deg(b) + 1 coefficients). 3. Verify no truncation occurs on the result. 4. Test with known polynomial pairs and verify: (a) result evaluates correctly at random points, (b) result degree matches deg(a) + deg(b). 5. Test edge cases: multiplying by degree-0 polynomial (constant), multiplying by monic polynomial of degree 1 (x - r form). 6. Verify the leading coefficient of result equals product of leading coefficients of inputs.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0015, Primary Element: SG-009. This is the post-condition component of PROP-0015. Incorrect degree in result would propagate errors through vanishing polynomial computations.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does interpolate_polynomialcoeff (SG-011) reject duplicate x-values to prevent division by zero?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the interpolate_polynomialcoeff function (SG-011). 2. Verify an explicit check for duplicate x-values exists, either: (a) explicit uniqueness assertion, or (b) detection of zero denominator during weight_adjustment computation. 3. Test with intentionally duplicated x-values and verify the function rejects/crashes rather than returning incorrect results. 4. Trace upstream: identify how cell_indices from batch verification (SG-015) are transformed into interpolation x-values. 5. Verify cell index deduplication occurs BEFORE reaching interpolation. 6. Attempt to craft a batch verification input with duplicate cell_indices that bypasses deduplication to reach interpolation.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0018, Trust Boundary: tb-007, Primary Element: SG-011. Duplicate x-values cause (xs[i] - xs[j]).inverse() to attempt inversion of zero, crashing the node or producing silently incorrect results.
